bull_bear.body: Debt/Equity maintained below 0.5x; Focus on funding organic capacity expansion and green energy initiatives while preserving balance sheet strength.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Global geopolitical tariffs impacting exports (US/Mexico duties); Delay in mandatory ABS regulation implementation; Aluminum price volatility affecting reported margin percentages; Slower than expected ramp-up of new JV products.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly optimistic ('bright future'), confident in mid-teen growth outpacing industry, pragmatic about margin math regarding commodities, cautious on regulatory timelines (ABS).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'margin compression' is purely arithmetic (denominator effect) rather than operational deterioration; the company is effectively trading lower-margin wheel assembly volume for higher-margin braking/lightweighting mix, yet reported consolidated revenue growth looks muted due to the mix shift.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Key Ratios FY 2026: Debt-Equity 0.50, Avg. Debt-EBITDA 0.95 and RoACE 26.9%.
- Credit rating by Crisil: Long term AA, Short term A1+.
- Last 4 years CAGR stated at 20.0% Revenue, 31.9% EBITDA and 38.4% EPS.
- The deck states no dividend policy, payout, buyback or explicit capex-funding framework.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Largest manufacturer of 2W Advanced Braking Systems in India with ~50% market share
- High entry barriers from proprietary material formulations and in-house Engineering, Designing & Tool room capability
- Powertrain-agnostic product offerings across EV and Non-EV
- 5 technical collaborations and 3 Joint Ventures with global players
- Long-standing OEM relationships and an established Aftermarket franchise focused on Quality, Cost & Delivery
- 18 manufacturing facilities strategically located near customer plants enabling just-in-time delivery and supply-chain efficiency
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and global trade uncertainty — Management explicitly flags that ongoing geopolitical turbulence has increased global uncertainty, which may adversely impact the Company's general business environment (relevant given its export presence and reliance on imported/globally-sourced inputs and technology partnerships).
- Rising financial leverage from capex funding — The Company's own ratio-analysis commentary states the Debt-Equity ratio increased due to an increase in debt, mainly to fund capital expenditure, indicating growing reliance on debt to finance the ongoing capacity expansion programme.
- Legacy low-margin wheel-assembly exposure — Management describes a 'calibrated reduction in the low-margin wheel assembly business', implying this segment has historically diluted blended margins and that the wind-down itself is an execution item to manage.
- Dependence on continued favourable GST/tax policy tailwinds — The Company's demand outlook for both OEM and Independent Aftermarket volumes is explicitly linked to GST rate reductions and tax-policy support (including GST 2.0 reforms); a reversal or dilution of these policy measures would remove a stated structural demand driver.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Advanced Braking: +22% Q3, +12% 9M; ALPS: +36% Q3, +24% 9M; Safety Cables: +22% Q3, +10% 9M. Growth driven by GST cut (28% to 18%) gaining aftermarket share from grey market.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as "a leading Brand in 2W Braking Segment in India" and the "Largest manufacturer of 2W Advanced Braking System in India with ~50% market share", offering powertrain-agnostic products across Advanced Braking Systems, Aluminium Lightweighting Precision Solutions and Safety Control Cables.
- Claims "High entry barriers due to proprietary material formulations, in-house Engg, Designing & Tool room" plus a "Strong In-house R&D, Engineering and Design Centre".
- 35+ years experience in safety products and solutions; "Long standing relations with all top 2W ICE and EV customers", with stated relationship tenures of 33, 25, 24, 24, 23 and 19 years for its 2W customers.
- 5 Technical Collaborations and 3 Joint Ventures with world-class global players (Japanese non-asbestos brake shoe manufacturer 2001, HSH Safety Control Cable 2016, NUCAP Canada 2016, FRAS-LE Brazil 2018, LIOHO Taiwan 2024, AISIN Japan 2024, Kyushu Yanagawa Seiki Japan 2025, T D Holding GmbH / GEMO 2025).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Recognition] India's Best Managed Companies 2025 award by Deloitte; 13 awards for Excellence in Quality, 10 for Performance, 8 for Development and 6 for Cost Innovation.
- [Listing] Listed on NSE on 15 November 2023; Board is promoter-led (Kuldip Singh Rathee as Chairman & MD with Prashant Rathee and Aman Rathee as Joint Managing Directors) alongside five independent directors.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: ASK Automotive is one of India's leading manufacturers of safety-critical, performance-defining automotive components, spanning Advanced Braking Systems (ABS), Aluminium Lightweighting Precision Solutions (ALPS) and Safety Control Cables (SCC). It serves two-wheeler, passenger-vehicle and commercial-vehicle OEMs, a nationwide independent aftermarket network and overseas customers, with 18 manufacturing facilities located close to customer plants for just-in-time delivery.
business.title: What they do

business.body: - **Advanced Braking Systems (ABS):** Brake Shoe, Brake Pads, Brake Panel Assembly
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- ASK Automobiles Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly Owned Subsidiary (100%); designated a material subsidiary of the Company.
- ASK Fras-Le Friction Private Limited — JV: Joint venture with Fras-Le S.A., Brazil, for manufacturing and marketing brake pads/linings for commercial vehicles; ASK holds 49%, Fras-Le holds 51%.
- AISIN ASK India Private Limited — JV: Joint venture with AISIN Asia (Thailand) Company Limited and AISIN Automotive Haryana Private Limited for marketing and selling Independent Aftermarket (IAM) parts for passenger cars; ASK holds 51%.
- ASK GTD Control Cables Private Limited — JV: Joint venture with T.D. Holding GmbH (Germany), the technical-license holder of GEMO, for manufacturing, marketing and selling sunroof and helix control cables for passenger vehicles; ASK holds 49%, TDH holds 51%; yet to commence commercial operations.
- AISIN Automotive Haryana Private Limited — related party: Co-venturer of the AISIN ASK India Private Limited joint venture.
- A.P. Automotives Private Limited — related party: Entity in which directors of the Company and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence; counterparty for rent paid.
- AA Friction Materials Private Limited — related party: Entity in which directors of the Company and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence; counterparty for purchase of goods/fixed assets and job-work services.
- AHSAAS Trust — related party: The Company's philanthropic/CSR arm; established by Chairman & Managing Director Mr. Kuldip Singh Rathee and Non-Executive Director Mrs. Vijay Rathee, delivering programmes in healthcare, education, environmental sustainability, sport, skilling, rural development and women's safety.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin compressed ~30-40 bps due to aluminum price hike (denominator effect); Absolute EBITDA unaffected due to month-on-month pass-through mechanism. Ideal blended capacity utilization target is 80%.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Mid-teens for Q4 and FY27; Margin: ~13.4% (impacted by aluminum prices, absolute EBITDA stable); Order Inflow: Strong OEM projections for Q4; Capex: FY26 ~Rs. 500 Cr (incl. solar), FY27 ~Rs. 400 Cr.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Specific order book value not disclosed; Management cites 'strong projections from OEMs' for Q4 and confident ramp-up of new JVs (Ford, Taiwan, Japan) starting H2 FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New product launches in H2 FY27: Alloy Wheels (Japan/Taiwan JVs), Sunroof Cables. Ford exports resumed but impacted by tariffs. Solar power expansion (11.55 MW Rajasthan) to reduce opex.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Electrification: strengthen position in EV via aluminium lightweighting precision solutions and advanced braking technologies suited to EV platforms
- Expand global footprint: leverage export opportunities to diversify revenue base into new geographies and reduce geographic concentration risk
- Diversify product offerings: strengthen ABS and ALPS portfolio while increasing presence in passenger vehicle (PV) and commercial vehicle (CV) segments, reducing dependence on any single segment and expanding beyond two-wheelers
- Strengthen Independent Aftermarket (IAM): expand distribution network and channel engagement to increase IAM penetration through product availability, wider channel reach and focus on spares/replacement demand
- Innovation-led growth: strengthen design, R&D and engineering capabilities to build a pipeline of next-generation systems, advance material science/precision engineering and strengthen in-house design and simulation expertise
- Disciplined capital allocation: realign portfolio towards higher-margin, scalable, technologically differentiated segments (advanced braking systems, ALPS, safety control cables) alongside a calibrated reduction in the lower-margin wheel assembly business
- Strengthen global relevance through technical collaborations and joint ventures with global partners, enabling entry into new product categories across 2W, PV, CV and ICE & EV platforms
- Continue to advance the sustainability agenda through additional captive/group-captive renewable energy initiatives
- Dividend is paid out of the year's profits in accordance with the Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy; the Board recommends the final dividend each year for shareholder approval at the AGM. No buyback of equity shares was undertaken during the year and no amount was transferred to General Reserves. Related-party transactions are approved and reviewed by the Audit Committee on a quarterly basis (with prior/omnibus approval) as part of the Company's governance discipline around capital and related-party transactions.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: 3 plants, including one Joint Venture plant, are currently under installation and are expected to become operational by FY2027. Separately, to cater to increased demand from GST 2.0 reforms, the Company is in the process of installing 2 new facilities. During FY26, capital was deployed towards capacity expansion at the Karoli (Rajasthan) and Bengaluru (Karnataka) plants, along with automation, technology upgrades and debottlenecking; the Bengaluru plant achieved healthy utilisation ahead of schedule. On the renewable-energy side, the 9.9 MWp captive solar plant in Sirsa, Haryana (commissioned in 2025) is delivering expected results; a further 11.55 MWp captive solar plant in Bikaner, Rajasthan is under construction (MD&A/ESG section states expected operational Q1 FY2027, while the Chairman's message elsewhere in this bundle states Q2 FY2027); and Group Captive Renewable Energy projects aggregating 11.1 MWp have already been commissioned. Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems were enhanced at the Karoli and Bangalore 3rd plant facilities. On the JV/partnership side, ASK GTD Control Cables Private Limited (49% ASK stake, with T.D. Holding GmbH, the technical-license holder of GEMO) was incorporated in September 2025 to manufacture, market and sell Sunroof and Helix Control Cables for passenger vehicles, leveraging GEMO's design and manufacturing expertise. On the CSR side, the Vocational Training Centre at Jhajjar is under development with the building ready, expected to be operationalised in FY2027.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian economy grew 7.7% in FY26 (among fastest-growing major economies), with GDP growth projected at 6.6% for FY27, supporting continued investment activity
- Robust domestic demand aided by lower income tax and GST rates stimulated automobile sales and vehicle registrations
- Successive RBI repo rate cuts (repo rate reduced to 5.25% in FY26) lowered financing costs, making vehicle ownership more accessible for individuals and fleet operators
- Two-wheeler domestic sales grew 10.7%, driven by a revival in replacement demand following GST rate cuts, recovering urban consumption and resilient rural incomes aided by a normal monsoon
- Two-wheeler EV adoption rising, supported by the PM E-DRIVE scheme's subsidies (extended to July 2026) and expanding EV charging infrastructure
- GST on the Independent Aftermarket reduced from 28% to 18%, driving greater formalisation and affordability, expected to benefit organised players such as ASK at the expense of unorganised/grey-market participants
- Auto component industry turnover grew 12.7% YoY in FY26, with the aftermarket segment growing 9%, supported by domestic demand and localisation initiatives
- Global growth outlook remains uncertain due to shifting trade policies, tariff-related disruptions and the West Asia conflict, which could raise costs and disrupt supply routes
- India's expanding FTA network (nine major FTAs in six years, including the India-EU FTA) expected to enhance auto component export competitiveness and market access over time
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: ASK Automotive delivered record absolute profitability in Q3FY26 driven by volume growth and GST-led aftermarket share gains, though reported margins faced a denominator effect from rising aluminum prices. The strategic exit from low-value wheel assembly and upcoming launches in alloy wheels and sunroof cables position the company for sustained mid-teen growth despite export headwinds.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: India's largest manufacturer of two-wheeler Advanced Braking Systems (~50% market share), delivering powertrain-agnostic, EV-focused braking, aluminium lightweighting and safety control cable solutions to leading automotive OEMs.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ASK Automotive is one of India's leading manufacturers of safety-critical, performance-defining automotive components, spanning Advanced Braking Systems (ABS), Aluminium Lightweighting Precision Solutions (ALPS) and Safety Control Cables (SCC). It serves two-wheeler, passenger-vehicle and commercial-vehicle OEMs, a nationwide independent aftermarket network and overseas customers, with 18 manufacturing facilities located close to customer plants for just-in-time delivery.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- ASK Automobiles Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly Owned Subsidiary (100%); designated a material subsidiary of the Company.
- ASK Fras-Le Friction Private Limited — JV: Joint venture with Fras-Le S.A., Brazil, for manufacturing and marketing brake pads/linings for commercial vehicles; ASK holds 49%, Fras-Le holds 51%.
- AISIN ASK India Private Limited — JV: Joint venture with AISIN Asia (Thailand) Company Limited and AISIN Automotive Haryana Private Limited for marketing and selling Independent Aftermarket (IAM) parts for passenger cars; ASK holds 51%.
- ASK GTD Control Cables Private Limited — JV: Joint venture with T.D. Holding GmbH (Germany), the technical-license holder of GEMO, for manufacturing, marketing and selling sunroof and helix control cables for passenger vehicles; ASK holds 49%, TDH holds 51%; yet to commence commercial operations.
- AISIN Automotive Haryana Private Limited — related party: Co-venturer of the AISIN ASK India Private Limited joint venture.
- A.P. Automotives Private Limited — related party: Entity in which directors of the Company and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence; counterparty for rent paid.
- AA Friction Materials Private Limited — related party: Entity in which directors of the Company and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence; counterparty for purchase of goods/fixed assets and job-work services.
- AHSAAS Trust — related party: The Company's philanthropic/CSR arm; established by Chairman & Managing Director Mr. Kuldip Singh Rathee and Non-Executive Director Mrs. Vijay Rathee, delivering programmes in healthcare, education, environmental sustainability, sport, skilling, rural development and women's safety.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian economy grew 7.7% in FY26 (among fastest-growing major economies), with GDP growth projected at 6.6% for FY27, supporting continued investment activity
- Robust domestic demand aided by lower income tax and GST rates stimulated automobile sales and vehicle registrations
- Successive RBI repo rate cuts (repo rate reduced to 5.25% in FY26) lowered financing costs, making vehicle ownership more accessible for individuals and fleet operators
- Two-wheeler domestic sales grew 10.7%, driven by a revival in replacement demand following GST rate cuts, recovering urban consumption and resilient rural incomes aided by a normal monsoon
- Two-wheeler EV adoption rising, supported by the PM E-DRIVE scheme's subsidies (extended to July 2026) and expanding EV charging infrastructure
- GST on the Independent Aftermarket reduced from 28% to 18%, driving greater formalisation and affordability, expected to benefit organised players such as ASK at the expense of unorganised/grey-market participants
- Auto component industry turnover grew 12.7% YoY in FY26, with the aftermarket segment growing 9%, supported by domestic demand and localisation initiatives
- Global growth outlook remains uncertain due to shifting trade policies, tariff-related disruptions and the West Asia conflict, which could raise costs and disrupt supply routes
- India's expanding FTA network (nine major FTAs in six years, including the India-EU FTA) expected to enhance auto component export competitiveness and market access over time

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: 3 plants, including one Joint Venture plant, are currently under installation and are expected to become operational by FY2027. Separately, to cater to increased demand from GST 2.0 reforms, the Company is in the process of installing 2 new facilities. During FY26, capital was deployed towards capacity expansion at the Karoli (Rajasthan) and Bengaluru (Karnataka) plants, along with automation, technology upgrades and debottlenecking; the Bengaluru plant achieved healthy utilisation ahead of schedule. On the renewable-energy side, the 9.9 MWp captive solar plant in Sirsa, Haryana (commissioned in 2025) is delivering expected results; a further 11.55 MWp captive solar plant in Bikaner, Rajasthan is under construction (MD&A/ESG section states expected operational Q1 FY2027, while the Chairman's message elsewhere in this bundle states Q2 FY2027); and Group Captive Renewable Energy projects aggregating 11.1 MWp have already been commissioned. Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems were enhanced at the Karoli and Bangalore 3rd plant facilities. On the JV/partnership side, ASK GTD Control Cables Private Limited (49% ASK stake, with T.D. Holding GmbH, the technical-license holder of GEMO) was incorporated in September 2025 to manufacture, market and sell Sunroof and Helix Control Cables for passenger vehicles, leveraging GEMO's design and manufacturing expertise. On the CSR side, the Vocational Training Centre at Jhajjar is under development with the building ready, expected to be operationalised in FY2027.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
